title: Implement "Artwork Collections" Feature via Data Layer Abstraction
description: The CanvasPulse Dashboard currently allows artists to manage individual artworks. The next major feature is to introduce 'Collections', allowing users to group multiple artworks into named galleries. This task is complex because the existing data access layer is tightly coupled to the 'Artwork' model. This task will be performed over three distinct development sessions, requiring the agent to first refactor the core data layer, then build the new feature on top of the refactored foundation, and finally integrate and test the complete functionality. The agent must retain context between sessions to succeed.

project_spec.name: CanvasPulse Dashboard
project_spec.description:
CanvasPulse Dashboard is a medium-sized, component-based web dashboard written entirely in C that lets digital-art collectives and creative agencies monitor, curate, and showcase real-time creative metrics (live artwork uploads, collaborative sessions, likes, social buzz, color-palette trends, etc.). The application treats every visual element of the dashboard—panels, charts, and interactive art previews—as plug-and-play components that can be independently developed, tested, and hot-swapped, encouraging experimental UI layouts without touching core business logic.

The back-end core is decomposed into granular service, repository, and REST API layers that expose creative resources (artwork, project, palette, trend) through a clean, versioned interface. A micro web-server (Mongoose) handles HTTP/S while an authentication middleware orchestrates social log-ins (Google / GitHub / ArtStation OAuth), session management, and email-based notifications. Front-end assets (HTML5/CSS3 templates rendered with Mustache-C) are served responsively to desktops, tablets, and wall-mounted studio screens. The entire stack is designed for creative flexibility—teams can add new visualization widgets or data sources (e.g., sentiment analysis, 3-D preview) by dropping in new shared-object components without recompiling the monolith.
dependencies: libjwt + OpenSSL (JWT creation, encryption, social OAuth)
libuv (async I/O, background jobs, email dispatch)
